summary: Scoped FINTRACK-25 (Alert Justification Feedback Loop) into 7 acceptance criteria and 6 Gherkin scenarios (happy path, ceiling-exceeded edge case, dismiss-vs-justify distinctness, wrong-alert-type negative, cross-user IDOR negative, SQL injection security). Resolved the open matching-rule question from the original scope note by reading FINTRACK-22's actual LARGE_TRANSACTION detection code: justification is a per-(user, category) amount ceiling equal to the justified transaction's amount, directly mirroring the existing category+amount-based detection mechanism rather than inventing merchant-pattern matching (which Transaction's schema doesn't support today).
